turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve had progressively worsening shortness of breath for the past two months, mainly with activity and not at rest. I also have an occasional dry cough, but I haven’t had any fever, chills, or night sweats.

Do you have any chest pain, pressure, palpitations, or episodes of passing out?
Do you have any chest pain, pressure, palpitations, or episodes of passing out?
Patient: No, I don’t have any chest pain or pressure, and I haven’t noticed palpitations. I also haven’t had any episodes of passing out.
Do you get short of breath when lying flat, or do you wake up at night gasping for air?
Patient: No, I don’t get short of breath when I lie flat, and I haven’t woken up gasping at night.
Have you noticed any swelling in your legs or ankles?
Patient: No, I haven’t noticed swelling in my legs or ankles.
Do you smoke, or have you ever smoked?
Yes, I’ve smoked about a pack of cigarettes daily for the past 40 years.
Have you had any wheezing, or do you have a history of asthma or COPD/emphysema?
Patient: I don’t have a history of asthma or COPD, and I haven’t really noticed wheezing—mostly it’s just getting short of breath with activity and the occasional dry cough.
Have you had any unintentional weight loss, loss of appetite, or coughing up blood?
Patient: I haven’t had unintentional weight loss or loss of appetite, and I don’t cough up blood.
Have you had any occupational or environmental exposures, such as asbestos, silica, coal dust, birds, mold, or chemical fumes?

I haven’t had any known exposures to asbestos, silica, coal dust, birds, mold, or chemical fumes, either at work or at home. I’m not aware of any particular substances that would have regularly irritated my lungs.
Have you had any prior heart or lung disease, blood clots, recent surgery, long travel, or cancer?
Patient: I don’t have any prior heart or lung disease, and I haven’t had blood clots, recent surgery, or long travel. I also haven’t been told I have cancer.
How old are you, and have you noticed any change in your exercise tolerance compared with 2 months ago?
Patient: I’m 60 years old, and yes—my exercise tolerance has been getting worse over the past two months. I get short of breath sooner when I’m active than I used to.
Have you had any recent respiratory infection, and can you tell me if the shortness of breath is constant with exertion or comes in sudden episodes?

Doctor: Have you had any recent respiratory infection, and is your shortness of breath constant with exertion or does it come in sudden episodes? Patient: I haven’t had any recent respiratory infection. It’s more of a steady, gradually worsening shortness of breath when I’m active, not sudden episodes.

[DDX] COPD/chronic bronchitis or emphysema, lung cancer, interstitial lung disease, coronary artery disease with exertional anginal equivalent, pulmonary hypertension

Most likely is smoking-related COPD/emphysema given age 60, 40-pack-year smoking history, progressive exertional dyspnea, and chronic dry cough without infectious symptoms.

Other important possibilities:
- Lung cancer: smoking history and new progressive dyspnea make this important even without weight loss or hemoptysis.
- Interstitial lung disease: can cause gradual exertional dyspnea and dry cough, though no clear exposure history.
- Coronary artery disease: exertional dyspnea can be an anginal equivalent even without chest pain.
- Pulmonary hypertension: can present with progressive exertional dyspnea without edema early on.

This would need in-person evaluation with vitals and oxygen saturation, lung and heart exam, chest X-ray, ECG, and likely spirometry; depending on findings, CT chest and labs may also be needed. If symptoms suddenly worsen, or if you develop chest pain, fainting, blue lips, or shortness of breath at rest, seek urgent care immediately.
